fact: The World Bank diagnostic says the Ministry of Justice, with UNICEF, launched the digital civil registry pilot SIREC in late 2018 exclusively in the capital Malabo, and that funding to expand the digital registry to the mainland is lacking; no office count is given.

The World Bank diagnostic says the SIREC pilot in Malabo allows the digital registration of new births, describes the platform as the one developed to collect new births and deaths, and reports UNICEF as saying it is operational and functions well (no date given; dated to the document's published year).
The World Bank diagnostic says the Ministry of Justice is responsible for civil registration and vital statistics and launched SIREC in late 2018, in collaboration with UNICEF.

The World Bank diagnostic says funding to expand the digital registry to the mainland is currently lacking and names no budget line or funder for SIREC beyond UNICEF's collaboration and support (no date given; dated to the document's published year).

The national statistics strategy for 2022-2026, which carries a budget annex, sets as expected result 1.1.6 a civil registry system established and vital statistics produced, measured by the percentage of progress in implementing the civil registry system, with INEGE named against it; the passages do not say what the system does or where (no date given; dated to the document's published year).

fact: UNICEF's Representative says the Sistema Informatizado del Registro Civil (SIREC) was put into service in December 2018 through the Ministry of Justice, with the support of UNICEF and the European Union and the collaboration of CNIAPGE.

UNICEF's Representative says that, in modernising the Central Registry Centre under SIREC, 192,000 birth records covering 1980 to 2019 were converted to digital form and 20,000 new records were digitised; deaths are not mentioned (stated in a speech of 16 June 2021).

UNICEF's CRVS profile, compiled from December 2016 to November 2017, gives the processing of birth, marriage and death registration as manual, on paper, at civil registrars' offices, mayors' offices, other district or local authorities and provincial birth registration centres; the registration points send their record books to the central birth office, which processes and files them on paper only.
system: Civil registration (Central Register of Notaries, Ministry of Justice, Worship and Correctional Institutions)
